title: Letting running containers keep their image through a deploy
text: Once Durable Object scheduling is in, shall I stop restarting running containers at a deploy? A visitor would keep their server until it sleeps after 10 idle minutes, and the next start would be on the new image. That is how a local Leaf server behaves when the plugin updates. An agent turn in progress would finish on the image it started on, so the restart-on-deploy design for cut-off replies isn't needed. The tab would follow its own server's runtime rather than the edge's release, which deletes the stop-at-deploy and the browser's release check. Someone who keeps working stays on the old image until they pause. It needs a dev check first: that a page from the previous image still loads its runtime files after the edge moves on. Do it after Durable Object scheduling Fewer mechanisms, and cut-off turns become rare. Keep stopping containers at a deploy A turn in progress at a deploy is still cut off.

Shall I move leaf.page's containers to Cloudflare's `durable_object` scheduling? Every production deploy today was followed by 2–5 minutes in which every container start failed with "Failed to start container". That happens because the Worker switches at once while the container image rolls out over minutes. Under the new policy, the session object picks the image each time it starts a container, so a new start always runs the current release. The window ends, and the store's release check goes. Cloudflare also reports starts about 6× faster. The `default` policy we use is now deprecated, and the replacement is in public beta. Cost: a new container application, which resets every visitor's records once. I'd build it, trial it on dev, then ship it. Build it, trial on dev, then ship Ends the failure window. Every visitor's records reset once. Hold off Each deploy keeps a 2–5 minute window of failed starts.

title: Trying Durable Object scheduling for leaf.page containers
text: Can I deploy a trial of Cloudflare's `scheduling_policy = "durable_object"` to leaf.page's dev application? Today a deploy switches the Worker and its Durable Object code at once, but container images roll over minutes later. That gap is why leaf.page stamps `Leaf-Release` on answers, swaps in the published page (`rollingOut`) and has the page store refuse another release ([PR #6457](https://github.com/max-sixty/leaf/pull/6457)). With the new policy, each Durable Object starts the image of its own Worker version, so the gap can't happen. The Durable Object would only replace a container left running from before the deploy, and it already holds the page record, so nothing is lost. That would let us delete the release stamp, `rollingOut`, the store's release check and the "still starting" 503s, and close the old-sample-link gap. The cost is a trial deploy to the dev application to check that `@cloudflare/containers` 0.3.7 lets the Durable Object pick the image, and what switching an existing application's policy does to visitors with open sessions. I recommend trying it. Deploy a trial to dev I switch the dev application's policy, test a deploy, and report back before touching production. Keep the release check PR #6457 stays the fix. The old-sample-link gap stays open.
